2026-10-29

  1. open the starwars dataset in tidyverse
library(tidyverse)
## ── Attaching core tidyverse packages ──────────────────────── tidyverse 2.0.0 ──
## ✔ dplyr     1.2.1     ✔ readr     2.2.0
## ✔ forcats   1.0.1     ✔ stringr   1.6.0
## ✔ ggplot2   4.0.3     ✔ tibble    3.3.1
## ✔ lubridate 1.9.5     ✔ tidyr     1.3.2
## ✔ purrr     1.2.2     
## ── Conflicts ────────────────────────────────────────── tidyverse_conflicts() ──
## ✖ dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter()
## ✖ dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag()
## ℹ Use the conflicted package (<http://conflicted.r-lib.org/>) to force all conflicts to become errors
data("starwars")
  1. create a graph showing the frequency of eye colors in the dataset.
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color))+ geom_bar()

  1. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color))+ geom_bar(fill = "mediumblue", color= "black")+ theme_classic()+ labs(x= "Eye Color", y= "Frequency", title = "Starwars Eye Colors" )

  1. Create a graph displaying information about character’s height in each homeworld.
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, homeworld))+ geom_boxplot()
## Warning: Removed 6 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).

  1. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
ggplot(filter(starwars, !is.na(homeworld)),aes(height, homeworld))+ geom_boxplot(fill = "turquoise1", color= "blue4", width = 0.4)+ theme_classic()+ labs(x= "Height", y= "Homeworld", title = "Starwars Height")

  1. Create a graph of character’s height by mass.
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass))+geom_point()
## Warning: Removed 28 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

7.Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.

ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height))+geom_point(shape = 8, color= "violetred")+ theme_classic()+ labs(x= "Mass", y= "Height", title= "Starwars Height By Mass")
## Warning: Removed 28 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

  1. Add gender as a third variable to your graph of height by mass.
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height, color=gender))+geom_point()
## Warning: Removed 28 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

  1. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
library(viridis)
## Loading required package: viridisLite
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height, color=gender))+geom_point()+ theme_classic()+ labs(x= "Mass", y= "Height", title= "Starwars Height By Mass")+ scale_color_manual(values = c("#FF33FF", "#3333CC"), na.value = ("#33FF99"))
## Warning: Removed 28 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).
